- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.22) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward more aggressively.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 2–5% for the following 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% higher), check if sentiment was bullish — if yes, reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with mean reversion.
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >10% lower), check if sentiment was bearish — if yes, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- Model tends to lag in early days of a new trend; for forecasts 1–3 days ahead, add 1–2% to forecast if sentiment is trending upward.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, model often overfits short-term noise; apply smoothing or use 7-day moving average to reduce overreaction.
